caption: The drawing depicts a symmetrical architectural façade with decorative elements. The structure is composed of an upper and a lower section, both delineated by horizontal bands. The background color is mostly beige or light tan. The upper section features a large arch at the center, outlined in red with a blue interior, containing a beige-colored bird in flight. On either side of the central arch are two rectangular brown panels, each framed with blue, red, and green decoration, and topped with fan-shaped red and blue motifs. The central area between the brown panels has a white background with green, red, and turquoise floral motifs arranged symmetrically around a black cross-shaped form. The lower section is defined by a broad band of alternating colored rectangles (primarily red, green, yellow, and white) just below the upper section. Below this, there are three large vertical brown panels, mirroring those above and also framed with blue and red accents. In the center of the lower section, there is an archway with a red border containing a blue and white vertically-striped curtain, adorned with red and black floral patterns. The bottom of the image shows just a hint of a tan-colored floor or platform. The entire composition uses distinct outlines in black, giving a stylized and graphical appearance to the various elements.
title: Plate 5: Main Altarpiece, Santa Cruz: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
